title: UPI Collect Request Fraud
howItWorks: The scammer claims to be sending you money — often while pretending to buy something you're selling online, or refunding a payment — but actually sends a 'collect' request instead. If you enter your UPI PIN to 'receive' it, money is debited from your account instead of credited.
redFlags: Any request that asks you to enter your UPI PIN to 'receive' money
Urgency around an online marketplace sale or a promised refund
A payment request appearing right after you list something for sale
whatToDo: Remember: a UPI PIN is only ever needed to send money, never to receive it
If a 'collect' request appears, decline it and verify with the other party through a separate channel
If you already entered your PIN, contact your bank immediately and report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930

title: Screen-Sharing Remote Access Scam
vector: Phone call posing as bank/customer support
howItWorks: A caller posing as bank or company support asks you to install a remote-access app (like AnyDesk or similar) to 'fix' a pending transaction or account issue. Once installed, the caller can see your entire screen, including OTPs and banking passwords, and can act as if they were physically holding your phone.
redFlags: Any unsolicited call asking you to install a screen-sharing or remote-access app
Pressure to act immediately to 'resolve' a transaction
Being asked to read out an OTP or PIN while a screen-share session is active
whatToDo: Never install a remote-access app at the request of an unsolicited caller
Hang up and call your bank back using the number on your card or official website, not a number the caller gives you
If you already installed one, disconnect from the internet immediately, uninstall the app, and contact your bank to freeze the account

title: "Digital Arrest" Scam
vector: Phone or video call posing as law enforcement
howItWorks: Fraudsters pose as police, CBI, or customs officials over a phone or video call, claiming you are under investigation or 'digital arrest' for money laundering or a similar crime, and demand payment to make the case go away.
redFlags: Any claim that you can be arrested or investigated over a phone or video call
Demands for immediate payment to avoid arrest
Instructions to stay on the call and not tell anyone ('secrecy' pressure)
whatToDo: Know this fact cold: no Indian law enforcement agency conducts an arrest or investigation via WhatsApp, Skype, or Zoom
Hang up — do not engage, pay, or share any personal/financial details
Report the call at cybercrime.gov.in or call the 1930 helpline

title: Vishing & Fake KYC Update Calls
vector: Phone call posing as bank/telecom/tax official
howItWorks: Callers pretend to be from a bank, telecom provider, or income-tax department, claiming your KYC has expired or your account will be blocked, and use urgency or fear to extract your OTP, card details, or Aadhaar information.
redFlags: Any call claiming your account/SIM will be blocked unless you act immediately
A request for your OTP, PIN, or full card number over a call
A caller who already seems to know some of your details, used to build false trust
whatToDo: Banks and telecom providers never ask for your OTP or PIN over a call
Hang up and contact the organization directly using their official number
Report suspicious numbers at cybercrime.gov.in

title: QR Code Swap Fraud
vector: Physical QR code tampering at shops
howItWorks: A fraudulent QR sticker is placed over a legitimate merchant's payment QR code at a shop or stall. Customers scan what looks like the store's usual QR code, but the payment goes to the scammer's account instead.
redFlags: A QR code sticker that looks slightly misaligned, newer, or different from the merchant's usual signage
The payee name shown after scanning doesn't match the shop name
Any QR code in a location where tampering would be easy (unattended stalls, unmonitored counters)
whatToDo: Always check the payee name displayed after scanning, before confirming payment
If it doesn't match the business name, cancel and pay by another method
Report a suspected swapped QR code to the merchant and to cybercrime.gov.in

title: Prepaid Task Scam
howItWorks: Victims are offered easy money for simple tasks like liking videos or rating hotels online. A few small real payouts are given first to build trust, after which victims are asked to 'invest' larger amounts for bigger returns — money that is then stolen.
redFlags: Any 'job' offering payment for trivially easy online tasks
Requests to deposit your own money to 'unlock' bigger earnings, after a few small real payouts
Pressure to recruit friends or family into the same scheme
whatToDo: Treat any request to pay money to earn more money as a red flag, regardless of past small payouts
Stop engaging and don't send any further funds once asked to 'invest'
Report the scheme and any transactions made at cybercrime.gov.in

title: Boss / Business Email Compromise Scam
vector: Email or messaging app posing as a senior executive
howItWorks: Criminals impersonate a senior executive or company leader, usually by email or a messaging app, and pressure an employee into making an urgent wire transfer or sharing confidential company information.
redFlags: An urgent request from 'leadership' that bypasses normal approval processes
Pressure to keep the request confidential or act before verifying
A sender address or number that's slightly different from the real executive's usual contact
whatToDo: Always verify unusual payment or data requests through a separate, known channel (call the person directly)
Follow standard approval processes even under time pressure
Report suspected attempts to your organization's IT/security team and to cybercrime.gov.in

title: Deepfake Voice Cloning Scam
howItWorks: Scammers use AI voice-cloning tools to imitate the voice of a family member, friend, or executive, then call claiming an emergency to pressure an urgent money transfer before the target can verify what's happening.
redFlags: An urgent, emotionally charged call asking for money transfer right away
Reluctance or excuses when asked to video call or verify identity another way
Requests to keep the situation secret from other family members or colleagues
whatToDo: Hang up and call the person back on their known number to verify independently
Agree on a family/team 'safe word' in advance for genuine emergencies
Report the incident at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930
